ID in ascending order. A request can match at most 10,000 API keys. Use
the providers or statuses filter to narrow larger result sets.

dates. The statuses filter applies to each API key's current status.

post.description:
Expects two headers:
- Authorization header formed from base-64 encoded client credentials as `Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>`
- `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

Required content body depends on authorization type method, as defined by `grant_type`.
- Authorization Code Grant (`grant_type=authorization_code`): `grant_type`, `code`, and `redirect_uri` are required. Request must happen after requested scopes have been approved and exchanged for authorization code.
- Refresh Token Grant (`grant_type=refresh_token`): `grant_type` and `refresh_token` are required. User must have previously obtained refresh token in authorization code flow.
- Client Credentials Grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`): `grant_type` is required. If `scope` is omitted, the access token has no scopes.

Expects an authorization header formed from base-64 encoded client credentials as `Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>`.

Content body must be form-encoded. Example:
```
curl \
    -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
    --data-urlencode 'token=$RAMP_API_TOKEN' \
    'https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/token/revoke'
```

x-enum-descriptions.CANCELED: The transfer has been canceled and will not be processed. This state is terminal and indicates the transfer was intentionally stopped, either by the customer or due to an operational decision.
x-enum-descriptions.COMPLETED: The transfer has successfully settled and reached its final state. Funds have moved as intended, and no further actions are required. Any subsequent issues would require a new transfer or reversal process.
x-enum-descriptions.ERROR: The transfer encountered a terminal error and could not be completed. This can happen due to issues like invalid account information or system errors. The transfer will need to be retried with corrected details.
x-enum-descriptions.INITIATED: A record of the transfer has been created in Ramp's system. The process of moving funds has started, but no external actions have been taken yet.
x-enum-descriptions.NOT_ACKED: Ramp did not receive an acknowledgment from the bank after submitting the transfer. The transfer may need to be retried or investigated for connectivity issues with the bank.
x-enum-descriptions.NOT_ENOUGH_FUNDS: The transfer could not proceed due to insufficient funds in the originating account. Additional funds need to be added to the account before re-attempting the transfer.
x-enum-descriptions.PROCESSING_BY_ODFI: The transfer file has been submitted to the Originating Bank (ODFI), and the cutoff time for same-day processing has passed. The ODFI has accepted the file and will proceed with sending it to the Fed.
x-enum-descriptions.REJECTED_BY_ODFI: The transfer was rejected by the ODFI before it was sent to the Federal Reserve. The rejection usually occurs due to formatting errors or invalid account information in the transfer file.
x-enum-descriptions.RETURNED_BY_RDFI: The transfer failed at the Receiving Bank (RDFI) due to an issue provided by the receiving bank. Common reasons include closed accounts or incorrect account numbers. This requires corrective action to resolve.
x-enum-descriptions.SUBMITTED_TO_FED: The transfer file has been sent to the Federal Reserve and is awaiting routing to the RDFI. The transfer is now in the Fed's hands and will soon be sent to the receiving bank.
x-enum-descriptions.SUBMITTED_TO_RDFI: The transfer has been delivered to the Receiving Bank (RDFI), and we are awaiting the final transfer of funds. This is the final step before the funds are made available to the receiving party.
x-enum-descriptions.UNNECESSARY: The transfer is for $0 and does not require processing through the ACH system. This is a terminal state, indicating no further actions are required.

patch.description:
Edits a native draft or submitted request as its owner. This action never
submits a draft; edits to a submitted request go through normal approval
reconciliation.

How each part of the body is applied:

- Top-level scalars (`name`, `currency`, `entity_id`, `start_date`,
  `end_date`): omit to keep the saved value. `start_date` and `end_date`
  accept `null` to clear.
- `field_answers`: omit to keep all answers. When present, the list is the
  complete set of API-editable answers: supported fields not listed are
  cleared and `[]` clears them all. File-upload answers are never touched.
- `accounting_field_selections` (request level): omit to keep. When present,
  the list is the complete set: enabled fields not listed are cleared and
  `[]` clears all.
- `line_items`: omit to keep all lines. When present, the list is the
  complete set of lines: a line with `id` is retained and updated, a line
  without `id` is created, and any existing line whose `id` is not listed is
  deleted. `[]` deletes every line (drafts only; a submitted request must
  keep at least one line).
- Every line must carry `unit_price` and `unit_quantity`, and `description`
  is written on every call: an omitted or `null` description clears it.
  Always re-send `id` and `description` for lines you want to keep.
- A line's `accounting_field_selections` and `custom_field_values` follow
  the collection rule: omit to keep the retained line's saved coding, send
  the complete list to replace it (enabled fields not listed are cleared),
  or send `[]` to clear it.

Returns the request detail. Request-level selections appear under
`purchase_order.accounting_tracking_category_selections`
(`tracking_category.uuid` = `accounting_field_id`,
`tracking_category_option.uuid` = `accounting_field_option_id`). Lines
appear under `purchase_order.purchase_order_line_item_log_entries` with
their `id`, `accounting_tracking_category_selections`, and
`custom_field_values` (`column_id` = `custom_field_id`).

X-Idempotency-Key is optional; reusing a key rejects the request rather
than replaying the original response.

Identity-owned invite / scheduled-invitation services:

``scheduled_enabled`` keeps the replaced group's value (true for new groups).

PayeeRenewalRecurringSettingsRequestBody.description:
Complete recurring reminder configuration.

``recurring_enabled`` is the on/off switch; the five ``recurring_*`` fields
describe the configuration. A configured but disabled object is paused (the
configuration is retained), while all-null configuration is only valid when
disabled.

recurring_cadence.description: Repeat frequency, required when recurrence is enabled. BIWEEKLY means every two weeks.

recurring_enabled.description: On/off switch. False with a configured recurrence pauses it; must be false when recurring_start_type is null.
recurring_enabled.title: Recurring Enabled

recurring_max_occurrences.description: Optional cap on the number of reminders in the series (occurrences 0..N-1 from the anchor). Null means unlimited.
recurring_max_occurrences.title: Recurring Max Occurrences

recurring_start_event.description: Contract event anchoring recurrence; required when configured. CONTRACT_START_DATE is only valid on perpetual contracts.

recurring_start_offset_days.description: Days relative to the contract event: negative before, zero on, positive after. Required when configured; must be 0 for CONTRACT_START_DATE.
recurring_start_offset_days.title: Recurring Start Offset Days

recurring_start_type.description: Anchor for recurring reminders; CONTRACT_EVENT is the only value. When null, all companion fields must also be null.

x-enum-descriptions.INITIATED: A record of the transfer has been created in Ramp's system. The process of moving funds has started, but no external actions have been taken yet.
x-enum-descriptions.NOT_ACKED: Ramp did not receive an acknowledgment from the bank after submitting the transfer. The transfer may need to be retried or investigated for connectivity issues with the bank.
x-enum-descriptions.NOT_ENOUGH_FUNDS: The transfer could not proceed due to insufficient funds in the originating account. Additional funds need to be added to the account before re-attempting the transfer.
x-enum-descriptions.PROCESSING_BY_ODFI: The transfer file has been submitted to the Originating Bank (ODFI), and the cutoff time for same-day processing has passed. The ODFI has accepted the file and will proceed with sending it to the Fed.
x-enum-descriptions.REJECTED_BY_ODFI: The transfer was rejected by the ODFI before it was sent to the Federal Reserve. The rejection usually occurs due to formatting errors or invalid account information in the transfer file.
x-enum-descriptions.RETURNED_BY_RDFI: The transfer failed at the Receiving Bank (RDFI) due to an issue provided by the receiving bank. Common reasons include closed accounts or incorrect account numbers. This requires corrective action to resolve.
x-enum-descriptions.SUBMITTED_TO_FED: The transfer file has been sent to the Federal Reserve and is awaiting routing to the RDFI. The transfer is now in the Fed's hands and will soon be sent to the receiving bank.
x-enum-descriptions.SUBMITTED_TO_RDFI: The transfer has been delivered to the Receiving Bank (RDFI), and we are awaiting the final transfer of funds. This is the final step before the funds are made available to the receiving party.
x-enum-descriptions.UNNECESSARY: The transfer is for $0 and does not require processing through the ACH system. This is a terminal state, indicating no further actions are required.
